text: If you're backed up on a GLP-1 and
eating less isn't helping, let me explain the
gut slowdown nobody warned me
about. Because once I understood it,
everything changed.
The shot was working and I was dropping
weight. But I felt like someone had filled
my gut with concrete and forgotten about it.
I'd eat a few bites at dinner and
feel like I'd swallowed a brick.
My jeans were getting looser but I was
still leaving the dinner table early.
Everyone kept telling me how great I looked,
and I couldn't explain it to anyone without
sounding dramatic.
Because from the outside, everything was
working. And I genuinely thought losing the
weight would fix it.
My doctor told me to add more fiber,
so I started mixing fiber powder into my
water every morning and eating
high-fiber everything.
I gave it a couple of months and
if anything I felt worse, still
waking up every morning with my gut full
of yesterday.
So I went to the pharmacy and got
MiraLAX. And that felt like
admitting something had genuinely gone
wrong. I stood in that aisle thinking
I shouldn't need this, but I was
desperate enough that I didn't care.
It helped a little, but the moment it
wore off I was right back where I
started. Something was still missing.
So I started doing a crazy
amount of research.
I must have read thirty articles,
forums, medical breakdowns, all of
it. And then I came across a
gastroenterologist who explained
exactly what GLP-1s do to the
gut. He explained it like this.
Your stomach is basically a muscle that
contracts and pushes everything forward.
But GLP-1s slow those contractions
down. Think of a river slowing to a
trickle. Everything behind it starts to back
up, food, waste,
gas with nowhere to go.
And all that pressure is what you're feeling
every day.
It wasn't a diet problem and it wasn't
something I was doing wrong.
It was the gut slowdown.
And my mind started racing.
Was this why the fiber never did anything?
Why MiraLAX only worked until it wore
off? So now I knew what was causing
it. But I had no idea what
actually fixed the slowdown.
One night I was up late scrolling a
GLP-1 support group on Facebook,
and a woman posted that she'd been backed
up for months on Ozempic until she
started using three specific ingredients
together. First was apigenin
from celery juice, which she said has been
shown to activate the receptors in the gut
wall that trigger those contractions.
Second was chlorophyllin, a plant
compound that binds gas-producing
compounds before they build pressure.
Third was a soluble prebiotic
fiber, and she was specific about the type.
The bulk kind in most fiber powders
and gummies just piles up in a gut
that's already slowed down, which is
exactly why mine made things worse.
She said that's why MiraLAX never stuck for
her either.
It's just pushing stuff out.
This is actually getting the muscle to start
moving again on its own.
She'd been on the shot for a year
and said it was the only thing that
ever worked.
She'd finally stopped dreading meals.
I almost kept scrolling because I'd tried the
celery juice thing back in
2019 and felt nothing.
But she said it doesn't work on its
own. You need all three together
in the right ratio.
She linked the one she used.
It's called Motilli, and it was the
only one I could find with all three
in the same gummy.
Everything else was just fiber with a
different label.
So I ordered it and changed nothing else.
Same shot, same eating.
Two gummies before breakfast with a glass of
water. The first week, honestly,
nothing happened.
But by week two I was sitting through
a full dinner with my husband without that
pressure building once, and by week
six I realized I hadn't thought about my
stomach in days.
That was me two months ago.
Now I get through dinner without planning my
exit, and I'm not mapping my day
around when I might feel okay.
So if you're on a GLP-1, losing the
weight, and still waking up every morning
backed up and wondering why nobody
warned you, this is why.
